issues.failure_explanation: Even assuming a valid frame theorem, its bounds concern the infinite analysis operator, not inversion of the sampled finite systems. For an overcomplete frame with independent finite subsets, take nonzero c in the synthesis kernel. Its finite truncations have norms tending to a positive limit while their synthesized functions tend to zero. Consequently, the finite synthesis maps have singular values tending to zero. The paper supplies no finite-section or sampling stability estimate overcoming this obstruction, and its implemented solver disables rank truncation. Existence of bounded-coefficient infinite expansions therefore does not imply the asserted computational stability.

failure_location.quote: Consequently, our method, where $\psi_j$ are used as basis functions in the MFS, enables a numerically stable approximation of solutions to Laplace boundary value problems, even when the solutions lack analytic continuation across the boundary.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish sampling, finite-section, and roundoff bounds for the stated solver, including any necessary regularization, or restrict the claim to infinite expansion stability and the reported experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The general numerical-stability conclusion for the implemented WMFS is unsupported, independently of whether its infinite frame construction is repaired. The reported experiments do not supply that guarantee.
issues.title: Infinite frame bounds do not establish stability of the finite numerical solver
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised computational guarantee requires a new numerical stability argument; otherwise a central guarantee type must be withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $k \geq 1$ and let $\delta \in (0,\infty]$. Consider $\varepsilon$-fine Whitney sets $\{q_j^\pm\}_{j = 1}^\infty \subset \Omega^\pm$ for $\Omega^\pm_\delta$ with respect to $\gamma$.
Let $\psi_j^\pm (w)= b^\pm_j(w - q_j^\mp)^{-(k+1)}$ be the corresponding normalized Lusin wavelets.
Let $b_j^+$ be the normalizing constant for $\psi^+_j$, so that $|b_j^+|^2 \simeq d(q_j^-)^{2k-1}m(B_j)$, where $B_j = B(q_j^-,\varepsilon d(q_j^-))$.

issues.failure_explanation: Because γ is compact, as |q|→∞ the normalized function b(q)(w−q)^{−k−1} approaches a normalized constant, up to a unimodular phase. Hence its inner product in absolute value with the normalized constant tends to 1. Any Whitney cover of the full unbounded exterior has infinitely many source points tending to infinity, so the claimed upper frame sum diverges for that constant function. The normalization actually satisfies |b(q)|² asymptotic to |q|^{2k+2}/length(γ), not d(q)^{2k+1}. The theorem also permits the same counterexample for finite δ because it does not require the exterior source set to be bounded.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use distance-based weights with decaying norms for the auxiliary unbounded exterior family, perform the compact-removal argument, and renormalize only a bounded exterior source set. Restrict the normalized theorem accordingly; its full-exterior version must instead use non-normalized weights.
issues.overall_effect: The normalized frame theorem is false as stated. The erroneous far-field normalization also defeats the compact-removal proof and the reduction from finite δ to δ=∞.
issues.title: Normalized far-field wavelets violate the upper frame bound
issues.why_classification: No normalized family covering the full unbounded exterior can satisfy the claimed Bessel bound. Repair necessarily changes the normalization or excludes the advertised full-exterior regime.
